title: [Audit] 🎛️ Command Center
description: Entry point for Cloud Audit Dashboards. KPIs, volume, actor risk and the live signal feed.

config.description: Every audited event in range, including machine noise. Compare with Signal to see how much the noise gate removes.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS `Total events · all traffic` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Events left after the noise gate removes health checks (cluster:monitor/main, elastic.maintenance), search-phase internals, connection_granted and bulk authentication_success.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | STATS `Signal events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Unique identities resolved as email, then API key name, then numeric user id.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS `Distinct actors` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor)

config.description: Distinct human identities (attributes.user.email). Machine traffic is excluded.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL | STATS `Human actors` = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.user.email)

config.description: Security configuration changes: API key invalidation, user profile writes, role edits. Any non-zero value deserves review.
Failed outcomes plus anonymous access denials — the first place to look during an incident.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.event.outcome == "failure" OR attributes.event.action == "anonymous_access_denied" | STATS `Failed events` = COUNT(*)

config.title: Audit volume by source · all traffic
config.description: Total audited events over time, split by originating service. Elasticsearch audits every transport action, so its volume usually far exceeds Kibana’s — and the Kibana slice is where most of the forensic value is.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), service = resource.attributes.service.name | EVAL source = REPLACE(service, "^serverless-", "")

**Noise gate is ON** — health pings, query internals and bulk `authentication_success`
are excluded; how much that removes varies by workload. Unfiltered totals live on **📊 Platform Volume**.

**Identity is resolved** — `user.name` is a numeric id, so panels fall back
`user.email` → `api_key.name`.

**Client IPs are real** — `source.ip` is the proxy; geography comes from
`network.forwarded_ip`.

*Hover any panel title for detail.*
config.title: How to read this suite
Actor footprint sized by volume, coloured by severity
config.description: The top 40 identities in range, in one block per kind: named API key (labelled by the KEY, with its owner — the principal that created it — on a further line when there is room, and in the tooltip), person (a real email address), cloud API key (an organisation-level Cloud key, which the audit stream records only by id and with no owner), and unattributed (a token or opaque principal). An identity is one tile even when its events disagree about its kind; it goes in the most specific block any of them supports. Area grows with the SQUARE ROOT of event volume, so one dominant identity cannot crush the rest into slivers, and the smallest identities get a minimum tile so every name stays readable — read exact counts from the tooltip. Colour is accumulated severity, the quantity the risk leaderboard ranks by.

config.title: Signal vs noise over time
config.description: Stream graph banding the firehose into signal, bulk authentication, query internals and infrastructure noise, with a readable volume axis. Shows why the noise gate exists.

config.title: Most frequent actions
config.description: Top audited actions after the noise gate, with the service that emitted them.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY action = attributes.event.action, service = resource.attributes.service.name | EVAL source = REPLACE(service, "^serverless-", "") | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Busiest identities
config.description: Who is generating signal traffic, and how varied their behaviour is. Identity resolves to an email, then an API key name, then a user id. Elasticsearch stamps an API key’s CREATOR’s email on every event the key emits, so any number of machines authenticating with one key resolves to one person’s name: where Via API key is filled in, that row is a credential’s traffic, not the person at a keyboard. Click an email to pin that identity across the suite.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action IN ("cluster:monitor/main", "elastic.maintenance") OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/search*" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action LIKE "indices:data/read/*point_in_time" OR attributes.elasticsearch.audit.action == "indices:data/read/open_reader_context")) AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("authentication_success","connection_granted"))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS events = COUNT(*), actions = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.event.action) BY actor, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.email | EVAL via_key = CASE(attributes.api_key.name != actor, attributes.api_key.name) | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Event categories · all traffic
config.description: ECS event categories over the whole stream, noise included. event.category is a multi-value array, so an event in two categories counts once in each and the bars sum to more than the event total.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY category = attributes.event.category | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 8

config.title: Live signal feed
config.description: The newest 200 signal events, newest first. Detail is the Kibana message, or the transport action on an Elasticsearch event. Open the Discover session to page further back or add columns.
